title: Seed-user credit splines — scratchpad
body:
Quick scratchpad — idea: give new users a shaped credit allotment that is more valuable when used early for high-velocity interactions, then tapers using a smooth spline instead of a step or exponential decay. Goal: increase activation (fast feedback loops) while limiting long tail abuse and smoothing revenue recognition for churny users.

Context / motivation:
- Traditional flat free credits often get hoarded; bursts of high consumption on day 1 followed by churn. We want front-loaded utility (encourage early product loops) but not infinite subsidy.
- Need something simple to explain to sales and CS: "you get X credits over Y days that slide down in marginal value".
- Must be cheap to implement in billing engine (prefer per-session multiplier + time window).

Core concept (heuristic):
- Allocate a nominal credit pool C_total (e.g., 5,000 token-equivalent credits) for a new account.
- Each credit has a time-since-signup weight w(t) between 0 and 1 given by a cubic spline anchored at (0=1.0, D_peak=1.0, D_fade=0.25, D_end=0.0). The effective usable credits at time t are credits * w(t).
- Practically we implement as per-day multiplier M[d] table for first 90 days (discrete approximation).

Why a spline:
- Smoothness avoids cliff complaints and weird edge-case hacks (e.g., sudden revocation).
- Can tune peak window (first 7 days) vs fade (days 8–30) and long tail (30–90).

Example parameters (back-of-envelope):
- C_total = 5,000 credits (1 credit ~ 1 input+0.5 output token unit; convert to tokens in billing later)
- Peak window D_peak = 7 days, during which M = 1.0 (full value)
- Fade window D_fade = 8–30 days, where M drops from 1.0 to 0.25 with cubic interpolation
- Tail window D_end = 31–90 days, linear drop to 0 by day 90

Effective early utility: if a user consumes 3k credits in first 7 days, that's 3k usable. The remaining 2k decays across weeks and may be used at 25–75% marginal value depending on timing.

Unit econ rough math (very approximate):
- Assume average cost to Redwood per 1k tokens served = $0.12 (mix of hosted model + infra amortization). This is the blended marginal cost including caching and batching.
- 5k credits ~= 5k token-equivalents -> cost ~ 0.005 * 120? wait compute: (5k tokens / 1k) * $0.12 = 5 * $0.12 = $0.60 per new account. That's attractive if LTV of converted user > $20.
- But worst-case heavy usage (e.g., streaming + long outputs) could push equivalent cost 3x — budget to ~ $1.80. Still okay for high-value ICP.

Credit tiling idea (operational):
- Instead of single pool, tile credits into buckets by day ranges: B0 (days 0–7): 3,000; B1 (days 8–30): 1,500; B2 (days 31–90): 500. Each bucket has a multiplier that maps to billing tokens.
- Advantage: simple ledger check (which bucket still has balance), deterministic expiration. Easier for CS to explain.

Edge cases / abuse mitigations:
- Require email + phone or credit card to claim the full B0; otherwise reduced B0 for lightweight signups.
- Rate limit per-minute to avoid bulk scraping.
- Tie some of the initial bucket unlocking to product-completing events (e.g., run a first question, connect integration) to avoid driving empty sampling.

Experiment plan (A/B):
- Control: flat 3k one-time credits (existing baseline).
- Variant A (spline): 5k total tiled as 3k/1.5k/0.5k with multipliers 1.0/0.6/0.2 and 90-day expiry.
- Metric: 7-day DAU, 14-day conversion to paid trial, cost per converted user, N-day waste (unspent expiring credits). Also qualitative CS feedback on clarity.
- Sample size: run for 6 weeks with new signups only; expect conversion lift of 8–12% to be meaningful.

Implementation notes (engineering):
- Billing model needs per-credit multiplier lookup by signup_age_days. Implement as small table + interpolation flag off for now to keep deterministic.
- UI: show "X credits available (higher value in first 7 days)" with tooltip linking to small page. Avoid exposing spline math.
- Data: instrument cohort-level credit usage per bucket, per-customer cost-to-serve, and conversion path.

Open questions / unknowns:
- What is acceptable cost per new paid account for our growth funnel? (finance target needed)
- Does smoothing improve perceived fairness vs simple bursts? Need qualitative testing with CS.
- How to handle referrals / invited accounts—do they get same tile? Potential for abuse.

Next steps / quick TODOs:
- Sync with finance to confirm per-1k token blended cost assumption (Riley + Aria).
- Product: mock banner text and FAQ copy (Noah).
- Engineering: feasibility check for tiled bucket implementation and analytics schema (ticket PRIC-4123).
- Run 6-week A/B with small percentage (5–10%) of new signups.

Scratch math notes / sanity check:
- If C_total = 5k and blended cost = $0.12 / 1k tokens -> cost/account = $0.60 nominal. If conversion rate uplift is +10ppts from baseline 2% -> 2.2%, CAC drop effective.
- If heavy model mix increases cost 3x -> $1.80/account. If LTV ~ $100, payback still favorable.

Freeform thoughts:
- Could combine with a "first-API-call" bonus multiplier to encourage SDK/CLI usage (unlock extra 1k B0).
- Consider co-marketing smaller B0 boosts for target accounts (sales-assisted).
- Long-term, make credit value aware of model family (e.g., consuming high-cost models draws from B0 at 2x multiplier) to protect unit economics while keeping perceived credit counts simple.

Unresolved: how to surface unused expiring credits so users feel value rather than frustration (email n-3 days? product prompt?).

End of scratchpad.

---
Notes to self: don't over-optimize lexicon for marketing until experiment completes. Keep copy simple: "Front-loaded credits to help you build quickly"."
